tips.cue: Varies with fruit type - fleshy fruits fully coloured and slightly soft, dry achenes brown and loose.
tips.collect: Pick fleshy fruit by hand; strip plumed achenes when they detach at a touch.
tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.cue: Umbels dry, mericarps brown and splitting into pairs.
tips.collect: Clip whole umbels into a bag.
tips.caution: This family includes poison hemlock and water hemlock, both lethally toxic. Do not collect from an umbellifer you have not identified with certainty.

tips.cue: Pappus (the fluff) has dried and begun to lift; heads look grey and open rather than green and tight.
tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.cue: Flower heads faded to rust or brown and papery; achenes dark and firm.
tips.collect: Rub heads between palms over a bag.
tips.handling: High chaff fraction is normal and mostly harmless for direct sowing.
tips.caution: Buckwheats hold dried flower heads for months after seed has dropped, so a brown head is not proof of full seed.

tips.cue: Florets straw-coloured, seed firm; awns twist when dry.
tips.collect: Strip the seed head upward through a closed hand into a bag. Ripe seed shatters readily - a light shake tells you.
tips.handling: Keep well ventilated. Awned grasses tangle badly; leave awns on unless you are sowing with a drill.

tips.cue: Capsules darkening and the first few have already exploded.
tips.collect: Bag branch tips or lay a sheet - the window between ripe and gone can be under a week.
tips.handling: Dry in paper bags and let them self-thresh. Needs hot water followed by cold stratification.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.
